# Setup

## Prerequisites

- A SLURM cluster with a GPU partition, or one machine with a GPU
- `python3` ≥ 3.11 and `conda` ≥ 24.7.1 (loaded by your site's `profiles/<site>/env.sh`;
  on Longleaf and Pioneer, a one-time Miniforge install; see
  [Cluster Reference](cluster.qmd#conda-version))
- CTCF peak files (CUT&Tag / ChIP-seq narrowPeak) for your samples, and optionally
  their Hi-C maps (`.hic`, `.mcool` or `.cool`)
- A genome FASTA with the same chromosome names as the peaks

There is no separate setup script: converting Hi-C, orienting CTCF sites,
and building conda environments are all steps of the workflow.

## 1. Samplesheet

`ChromSimSamplesheet.txt` is tab-separated, one row per experimental sample.
Two columns are required; the rest are free-form metadata:

| Column | Contents |
|--------|----------|
| `CTCF_Peaks` | CTCF peak file (narrowPeak/BED), or `NA` |
| `Hi-C` | Hi-C map to compare simulations against (`.hic`, `.mcool` or `.cool`), or `NA` |
| anything else | metadata (`Project`, `Cell_Type`, `Condition`, ...) |

```
Project  Cell_Type  Condition   CTCF_Peaks                Hi-C
STRS     HEK293T    condition1  data/control.narrowPeak   data/control.hic
STRS     HEK293T    condition2  data/sorbitol.narrowPeak  data/sorbitol.hic
```

Paths can be absolute or relative to the repo root. Using `data/<file>`
lets one samplesheet serve every cluster: each cluster links its own copies
into `data/` (next section). On a single cluster, absolute paths are simpler
and no linking is needed.

**Hi-C formats.** `.hic` is converted with `hic2cool`; from an `.mcool` the
`resolution` set in the config (1 kb by default) is copied out, so the file
must contain it; a `.cool` must already be binned at `resolution`. Without
Hi-C, write `NA` and leave `compare_hic` out of the conditions: the
simulations run as usual, without the comparison.

`fileNamesFrom` in the config lists the columns joined with `_` to name each
sample (the bagPipes convention). With `fileNamesFrom: ['Condition']` the
samples above are `condition1` and `condition2`.

### Linking the input files (optional)

Only needed when the samplesheet uses `data/<file>` paths. On each cluster,
link the files named in the samplesheet, and the genome FASTA named by
`genome`, into `data/` once, from the repo root:

```bash
SRC=/path/to/this/clusters/data
ln -s "$SRC"/STRS_HEK293_eGFP-YAP_CTCF_cont_0h_peaks.narrowPeak    data/
ln -s "$SRC"/STRS_HEK293_eGFP-YAP_CTCF_sorbitol_1h_peaks.narrowPeak data/
ln -s "$SRC"/YAPP_HEK293_eGFP-YAP_Cai_control_megaMap_inter_30.hic  data/
ln -s "$SRC"/YAPP_HEK293_eGFP-YAP_Cai_sorbitol_megaMap_inter_30.hic data/
ln -s /path/to/GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa                    data/
ls -lL data/
```

A link takes no space, so the large files stay where they are. `ls -lL`
follows the links and reports any that are broken. Everything in `data/`
except `data/README.md` is git-ignored.

## 2. Config

Edit `config/ChromSimConfig.yaml`. The fields most runs change:

| Field | What to set |
|-------|-------------|
| `samplesheet`, `fileNamesFrom` | Samplesheet path and naming columns |
| `outputDir` | Where every output goes (default `output`; a relative path goes under `$CHROMSIM_OUTPUT_ROOT` if set) |
| `genome`, `genome_assembly` | FASTA for FIMO and its assembly name |
| `ctcf_motif` | JASPAR motif ID (or a local MEME file), FIMO threshold, flank, what to do with unoriented peaks |
| `loci` | Simulated windows (one or more): whole-number bp coordinates on the `resolution` grid; see [choosing a window](configuration.qmd#choosing-a-window) |
| `tiling` | Spacer per copy (`padding`) and chain length (`chain_size`); copies per locus are worked out |
| `polysim` | Simulation model settings (bootcamp defaults) |
| `conditions` | One entry per simulation; `ctcf_type` / `compare_hic` name samples |
| `n_replicates`, `n_shards` | Simulations per condition and GPU jobs per simulation |
| `condaEnvs` | Env file, env name, or env path for each rule group |

See [Configuration](configuration.qmd) for every field.

## 3. Compute site

Pick your site's profile folder: `profiles/longleaf` (UNC, the config's
default `hpcProfile`), `profiles/pioneer` (Case Western), `profiles/local`
(no scheduler), or your own copy of `profiles/slurm-template`. On any
cluster other than the default, set it once in `~/.bashrc`, together with
where output should go:

```bash
echo 'export CHROMSIM_PROFILE=profiles/pioneer' >> ~/.bashrc
echo 'export CHROMSIM_OUTPUT_ROOT=/scratch/pioneer/users/$USER/ChromSimPipe' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
```

See [Cluster Reference](cluster.qmd#per-cluster-settings).

## 4. Conda environments

`condaEnvs` in the config tells Snakemake which environment each rule runs in.
By default these are the files in `envs/`, which Snakemake builds on first
use. Build them once per cluster before the first run, on a compute node
(the build needs more memory than login nodes or the launcher job allow,
and takes ~30 min):

```bash
srun -N 1 -n 1 -c 4 --mem=16g -t 3:00:00 --pty /bin/bash   # add -p <partition>
bash ChromSimPipe.sh --conda-create-envs-only
exit
```

`envs/cohesin_sim.yml` pins `cuda-version=12.4` (CUDA 13 does not support
Pascal or Volta GPUs) and `numpy<2`, and uses only conda-forge and bioconda.
Editing an env file gives it a new hash, so Snakemake builds a fresh
environment; delete the old one under `.snakemake/conda/` to free space.

To reuse environments you already built, give their name or path instead:

```yaml
condaEnvs:
  sim:  '~/.local/share/mamba/envs/cohesin_sim'
  ctcf: '~/.local/share/mamba/envs/ctcf_extraction'
```

## 5. Email (optional)

```bash
export CHROMSIM_EMAIL=you@university.edu   # e.g. in ~/.bashrc
```

You then get one email when a run starts, finishes, or fails. See
[Running](running.qmd#email-notifications) for the `notify:` options.

## 6. Test the setup

Before the first full run on a new cluster, run the 10-job test config:

```bash
bash ChromSimPipe.sh --configfile config/ChromSimConfig.test.yaml -n
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh --configfile config/ChromSimConfig.test.yaml
```

See [Running](running.qmd#test-run-first).

## Troubleshooting setup

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `Samplesheet ... has no 'CTCF_Peaks' column` | Header typo, or spaces instead of tabs | Use tabs and the exact headers `CTCF_Peaks`, `Hi-C` |
| `Duplicate sample name` | `fileNamesFrom` columns don't tell rows apart | Add a column to `fileNamesFrom` |
| `Condition ctcf_type '...' has no CTCF_Peaks` | Condition names a sample that isn't in the samplesheet | Check sample names against `output/{runName}_ChromSimSamplesheet.txt` |
| `must be multiples of resolution` | A locus window off the 1 kb grid | Use the aligned window the message suggests |
| `region_end ... is past the end of` | A locus window beyond the chromosome's end | Use at most the end the message gives |
| `chromosome ... is not in` | `chrom` is named differently from the genome (`chr2` vs `2`) | Match the genome's chromosome names |
| `Error running conda info` | conda not on `PATH` | Fix the conda line in `profiles/<site>/env.sh` |
